title: LongRoPE: Extending LLM Context Window Beyond 2 Million Tokens
content_text: We study position interpolation and scaling to extend context length. Experiments on retrieval and summarization show stable perplexity up to 2M tokens with tuning.

analysis_output.summary: Proposes a recipe (scaling + fine-tuning) to push transformer context to millions of tokens while keeping quality on long-range tasks.
key_findings: Position scaling plus targeted long-context finetuning preserves perplexity on long sequences.
Gains are strongest on retrieval-style tasks; summarization benefits depend on chunking.
Reports ablations on scaling factors and training mix.
analysis_output.critique: Claims rely on specific training setup; evaluation tasks are limited and may not reflect real multi-doc reasoning. Missing cost/latency discussion.
analysis_output.context: Related to RoPE scaling, position interpolation, and long-context LLM work from Anthropic/OpenAI; useful for RAG and codebase analysis.

title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
content_text: Paper describing Llama 2 training, data mix, safety tuning and chat fine-tuning. Includes evals vs other open models and a safety policy description.

analysis_output.summary: Describes Meta’s Llama 2 base and chat models, including supervised fine-tuning and RLHF-style alignment, with evaluations and safety-focused release choices.
key_findings: Chat variants outperform base on helpfulness benchmarks after alignment.
Training details emphasize data filtering and safety policies.
Includes extensive evaluation across reasoning, coding, and toxicity metrics.
analysis_output.critique: Some training details are high level; external reproducibility is limited. Benchmark-driven claims may not transfer to domain tasks.
analysis_output.context: Common baseline for open LLM comparisons; relevant to alignment, dataset curation, and deployment safety considerations.

title: Reducing Hallucinations in RAG with Verifier Models
content_text: Abstract: We introduce a lightweight verifier that scores answer spans against retrieved passages, reducing unsupported claims in RAG pipelines across QA tasks.

analysis_output.summary: Presents a verifier component for RAG that flags unsupported generations using passage-level entailment signals, improving factuality without big latency hits.
key_findings: Verifier scoring reduces unsupported citations in open-domain QA.
Works best with multiple retrieved passages and explicit quote extraction.
Calibration enables thresholding for abstain/ask-clarify behaviors.
analysis_output.critique: Verifier depends on retrieval quality; may regress on creative tasks. Needs stronger analysis on adversarial passages and domain shift.
analysis_output.context: Fits into RAG guardrails alongside citation checking, constrained decoding, and post-hoc fact verification.

title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
content_text: We finetune 4-bit quantized LLMs with low-rank adapters. Memory savings enable 65B models on a single GPU while matching full finetune quality on instruction data.

analysis_output.summary: Introduces QLoRA: 4-bit quantization + LoRA adapters for efficient instruction tuning of large models with limited GPU memory.
key_findings: NF4 4-bit quantization preserves finetuning performance with big memory reduction.
Paged optimizers reduce memory spikes from optimizer states.
Adapter tuning reaches near full-finetune quality across instruction benchmarks.
analysis_output.critique: Throughput can be lower due to dequant overhead; benefits depend on kernel maturity. More results on non-English and long-context tasks would help.
analysis_output.context: Widely used for practical finetuning; complements PEFT approaches and quantized inference stacks.

title: RAG-Fusion: Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Query Generation
content_text: We generate multiple search queries from a prompt and fuse retrieved results to improve recall. Evaluated on multi-hop QA and long-form generation tasks.

analysis_output.summary: RAG-Fusion improves retrieval recall by generating diverse sub-queries, retrieving per query, then fusing results before generation.
key_findings: Multi-query retrieval boosts multi-hop QA accuracy by increasing evidence coverage.
Reciprocal-rank fusion is a strong, simple aggregation baseline.
Diversity constraints reduce redundant queries and improve latency/quality tradeoff.
analysis_output.critique: Extra retrieval calls increase cost; gains may vanish on already-strong retrievers. Needs analysis of failure modes when queries drift.
analysis_output.context: Useful for assistants using web search; pairs well with rerankers and citation-based answer formatting.

title: Benchmarking Local Search for Restaurant Discovery
content_text: PDF excerpt: We compare local search providers on precision of address/phone, opening hours correctness, and category recall. Dataset: 50 US cities, 12k POIs.

analysis_output.summary: Evaluates local search accuracy for POI discovery using field-level correctness metrics (hours, phone, address) across a multi-city dataset.
key_findings: Opening hours are the noisiest field; phone numbers are most stable.
Long-tail categories show higher omission rates across providers.
Regular refresh improves hours accuracy but increases duplicates without entity resolution.
analysis_output.critique: Limited geography (US only) and no seasonal analysis. Ground truth collection method is only briefly described.
analysis_output.context: Relevant to Brave local search auditing and deduplication strategies in POI pipelines.

title: DPO: Direct Preference Optimization for Language Model Alignment
content_text: We optimize a policy directly from preference pairs without a reward model. The objective is a simple classification loss derived from KL-regularized RL.

analysis_output.summary: DPO aligns LMs using preference pairs via a closed-form objective, avoiding separate reward model training while matching RLHF-style outcomes.
key_findings: Simple loss over chosen/rejected responses approximates KL-regularized RL objective.
Less engineering overhead than PPO-style RLHF pipelines.
Shows strong results on chat alignment benchmarks with stable training.
analysis_output.critique: Still relies on preference data quality; tradeoffs vs reward modeling under distribution shift are underexplored.
analysis_output.context: Useful for chat assistants where alignment iterations need to be fast and reproducible.

title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
content_text: We present selective state space models enabling linear-time sequence processing. Benchmarks show competitive language modeling and better long-context scaling vs attention.

analysis_output.summary: Mamba introduces selective state-space layers that provide linear-time sequence modeling, offering a non-attention alternative for long contexts.
key_findings: Selective gating improves expressivity over prior SSMs.
Linear-time computation scales better with sequence length than attention.
Shows strong results on language modeling and long-context synthetic tasks.
analysis_output.critique: Practical gains depend on optimized kernels; some tasks still favor attention for precise token-to-token interactions.
analysis_output.context: Relevant to assistants needing long-context processing under tight latency budgets; complements hybrid attention/SSM designs.

title: A Practical Guide to Citation Grounding in Web-Connected Assistants
content_text: We propose a citation grounding checklist: quote extraction, span-to-source alignment, and refusal when sources are insufficient. Includes failure taxonomy and UI patterns.

title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
content_text: We scale autoregressive language models to 175B parameters and study zero-, one-, and few-shot behavior across NLP tasks. Shows emergent in-context learning.

title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
content_text: We augment an LM with API call annotations generated automatically, enabling tool use without human demonstrations. Evaluated on QA and calculator-like tasks.

analysis_output.summary: Toolformer shows how an LM can self-generate tool-use training data by inserting API call candidates and filtering by likelihood improvement.
key_findings: Self-supervised tool annotation reduces dependence on human-labeled demonstrations.
Filtering criterion selects calls that improve next-token likelihood.
Demonstrates improvements on tasks benefiting from search/calculation APIs.
analysis_output.critique: API set is narrow and curated; safety and misuse risks are not deeply evaluated. Real-world reliability depends on tool error handling.
analysis_output.context: Directly relevant to orchestrating Brave search + Gemini analysis; supports designs where the model learns when to search.
